texts.facts: ( i) The plaintiff is a public limited company incorporated under the provisions of Companies Act, 1956 and is engaged in the business of manufacturing tin containers used for packaging. The defendant no. 1 is a private limited company engaged in the business of packing of fruit pulp and defendant no(s) 2 and 3 are its Directors. The plaintiff maintained a mutual open running current account to record transactions of all the bills raised towards the supplied made to defendants. As per the said account, a sum of Rs.16,64,630/ is due and payable by the defendants to the plaintiff. Since the defendants have failed and neglected to pay the aforesaid sum, they are also liable to pay interest @18% p.a. on said sum which comes to Rs.4,01,051/ till 10.04.2015. The defendants were also liable to submit/ deposit Sales Tax/ C Forms which they failed to do, the defendants are also liable to pay a sum of Rs.3,69,106/ towards Sales Tax alongwith interest of Rs.1,20,041/ @ 2% per month till 31.03.2015. (iii) The plaintiff issued legal demand notice dt. 20.10.2014. Pursuant to same, defendants paid a sum of Rs.1,00,000/ to the plaintiff on 02.04.2015. Thus, the defendants are indebted in all for a sum of Rs.25,54,828/ to the plaintiff alongwith pendente lite and future interest @18% p.a. (iv) There is one table with regard to the goods supplied in para no. 3, the outstanding amount and the sales tax liability are reflected in para no. 6 & 10 respectively which I am quoting as hereunder: Registered Office At vs M/S Makarwa Foods Pvt. The breakup is also as hereunder: "(1) Principal outstanding amount with interest Rs.20,65,681/ (details given in para 6) (2) Nondelivery of Sales Tax Forms 'C' with interest (details given in para 10) Rs.4,89,147/ TOTAL Rs.25,54,828/" Suit no. 9166/16 Page no. 4 of 10 Hindustan Tin Works Ltd. vs. M/s Makarwa Foods Pvt. Ltd. & ors As such the present suit. 2. The defendants had filed their joint written statement taking following pleas in the preliminary objections: (i) There existed an arbitration clause as per Sales Agreement dated 15.01.2013, therefore, the present suit is not maintainable. (ii) The defendants had cleared all the approved bills for financial year 20122013 and 20132014 and had also provided sales tax 'C' Forms to the plaintiff. The factum Registered Office At vs M/S Makarwa Foods Pvt. Ltd on 11 February, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160250209/ 3 of up to date payments and supply of 'C' Forms to the plaintiff has been reflected in emails and other communications. (iii) The defendant has also paid an extra sum of Rs.1,00,000/ to the plaintiff. (iv) The bills mentioned by the plaintiff bearing no. 2217, 2249, 2322, 2460, 2588, 2667 and 2698 were where the supply was not as per the specifications, the products were not matching and standard laid down for food and packaging of fruit pulp under food standards and safety Act. These products were returned by the defendant. (v) The defendant company by way of emails expressed the deficiencies and the over rating done in the bills, including the interest charged which was not stipulated in the contract. But the plaintiff did not reply the same. (vi) On merits, the contentions of the plaintiff were denied in toto. Dismissal of the suit was sought for. Suit no. 9166/16 Page no. 5 of 10 Hindustan Tin Works Ltd. vs. M/s Makarwa Foods Pvt. Ltd. & ors 3. Replication to written statement was filed by plaintiff denying the contents made in the written statement and reaffirming and reiteration the averments of the plaint. In so far as the applicability of Arbitration Clause was concerned it was stated that the same is not made out in terms of the provisions of Arbitration & Conciliation Act, 1996, particularly Section 8 thereof. It was strongly denied that the goods supplied were not as per the specification or not in accordance with the standard of FSSAI Act. 4. In defence, the defendants did not examine any witness and DE was closed by order of the Court dated 30.10.2019 and matter was thereafter posted to final arguments.
